doc.title: Ray Conniff interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998

title: Still playing trombone on tours
summary: Conniff still plays Jack Teagarden-style trombone on tours and enjoys good music the audience can understand.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Well I think probably there’s a lot of song composers that are very fond of you also, because I’m sure some of them have gotten some royalties out of all the records you’ve sold, because of the great arrangements you’ve written of their music.

It’s been fun because I’ve been able to do what I’ve done all the years through the band days and the big band days and playing trombone — I still play trombone, when I go out on the tours I’ll play a little Jack Teagarden, I’ll play “Basin Street Blues,” or “I’ve Got a Right to Sing the Blues” or something. And I still have great musicians in the band. And it’s fun to play what I call good music, but still done in a way that the people that are out there listening and coming to the concerts can understand and enjoy as well.
